understanding: normalizeRemote accepts four narrowly defined kinds of git remote strings, rejects unsafe or unrecognized inputs before normal shape handling, and returns a credential-free canonical spelling used as the sole repository-identity key. It trims surrounding whitespace; removes schemes, credentials, ports, boundary slashes, and trailing case-insensitive .git suffixes; lowercases hosts; lowercases GitHub paths only; emits single-label hosts in scp form and local paths as file:<absolute path>; and must be idempotent.

cases.name: whitespace_only_is_rejected
cases.expected: Throws an Error whose message starts with "Unsupported remote: ".
cases.why_adversarial: The value is nonempty before the contract-required trimming step.
cases.defeats: A version that checks raw string length and consequently accepts a trimmed empty path.

cases.name: trimmed_option_is_rejected
cases.expected: Throws an Error whose message starts with "Unsupported remote: " and ends with "(looks like an option)".
cases.why_adversarial: The dangerous leading hyphen appears only after surrounding whitespace is removed.
cases.defeats: A version that performs the option check before trimming or only checks input[0].

cases.name: helper_detection_is_prefix_scoped
cases.expected: The first call throws an Error whose message starts with "Unsupported remote: " and ends with "(transport helpers are not allowed)". The second returns "example.com/team/ext::repo".
cases.why_adversarial: The same helper-like marker is dangerous at the trimmed input prefix but ordinary path data elsewhere.
cases.defeats: A version that either checks helpers before trimming or rejects every input containing "::" with an overbroad substring or regex test.

cases.name: url_userinfo_uses_last_at
cases.expected: Returns "github.com/org/repo" and does not include "alice" or "p@ss" in the result.
cases.why_adversarial: The password contains an @, so splitting the authority at the first @ invents the wrong host.
cases.defeats: A version that splits URL userinfo at the first @ or mistakes "ss@GitHub.com" for part of the path or host.

cases.name: scp_path_credential_is_refused_and_redacted
cases.expected: Throws an Error whose message starts with "Unsupported remote: "; the message must not contain "sekret".
cases.why_adversarial: The ordinary git@ login is valid, but a second @ in the first path segment represents a forbidden credential attempt and exercises redaction on failure.
cases.defeats: A version that strips every prefix through the last @, accepts scp passwords, or includes the full rejected input in its error message.

cases.name: host_option_after_userinfo_is_rejected
cases.expected: Throws an Error whose message starts with "Unsupported remote: ".
cases.why_adversarial: The host-leading hyphen is hidden behind valid-looking URL userinfo.
cases.defeats: A version that checks only whether the whole trimmed input starts with a hyphen and never validates the parsed host.

cases.name: windows_drive_is_not_scp_host
cases.expected: Throws an Error whose message starts with "Unsupported remote: ".
cases.why_adversarial: It nearly matches host:path, but the contract explicitly reserves a one-character host as a Windows drive letter; it is also not one of the accepted local absolute-path forms.
cases.defeats: A generic scp regex that accepts any non-slash text before the first colon.

cases.name: url_single_label_host_emits_scp_spelling
cases.why_adversarial: It combines trimming, a case-insensitive scheme, login removal, port removal, host lowercasing, case-preserving path cleanup, and URL-to-scp output conversion.
cases.defeats: A version that canonicalizes all URL inputs as host/path or lowercases every repository path.

cases.name: non_github_path_case_is_preserved
cases.why_adversarial: Host and suffix comparisons are case-insensitive, while this host's path is explicitly case-sensitive.
cases.defeats: A version that lowercases the entire normalized remote because GitHub paths are case-insensitive.

cases.name: local_forms_converge_without_case_folding
cases.why_adversarial: One local repository arrives through all three accepted routes, including two easily confused file URI spellings.
cases.defeats: A version with separate local-path branches that retain file://, emit differing slash counts, or lowercase a local filesystem path.

cases.name: single_label_slash_form_is_not_canonical
cases.expected: Throws an Error whose message starts with "Unsupported remote: ".
cases.why_adversarial: It looks like the accepted dotted-host canonical form and like a common two-segment shorthand, but has no dot in its host.
cases.defeats: A version that accepts every host/path-looking string and consequently mistakes org/repo-style shorthand for a remote.

cases.name: repeated_git_suffix_removal_is_idempotent
cases.expected: Returns "example.com/org/repo"; normalizing that returned value again also returns "example.com/org/repo".
cases.why_adversarial: Removing only one trailing suffix would initially produce another value that itself still requires normalization, violating the explicit idempotence invariant.
cases.defeats: A version that performs a single non-repeating replacement of one trailing .git suffix.

cases.name: git_suffix_alone_names_no_repository
cases.expected: Throws an Error whose message starts with "Unsupported remote: ".
cases.why_adversarial: The raw path is nonempty, but case-insensitive suffix removal leaves no repository name.
cases.defeats: A version that validates path nonemptiness only before cleaning or checks only the lowercase literal ".git".

contract_gaps.gap: The allowed host grammar is not defined beyond slash, dot, leading-hyphen, and one-character-host rules.
contract_gaps.why_it_matters: Implementations can disagree about IPv6 literals, trailing dots, underscores, Unicode/IDNA names, empty hosts, and other punctuation while all appearing consistent with the stated shapes.

contract_gaps.gap: The syntax and validity rules for [:port] are unspecified.
contract_gaps.why_it_matters: Empty, signed, nonnumeric, out-of-range, or whitespace-containing ports may be accepted and discarded by one implementation but rejected by another.

contract_gaps.gap: “Path cleaning” is not fully defined beyond removing boundary slashes and trailing .git.
contract_gaps.why_it_matters: Internal repeated slashes, dot segments, backslashes, and percent-encoded separators can normalize differently and therefore alter repository identity.

contract_gaps.gap: URL query strings, fragments, and percent-decoding behavior are unspecified.
contract_gaps.why_it_matters: Two implementations may treat ? and # as repository-name characters, discard them as URL components, or reject them, producing incompatible comparison keys.

contract_gaps.gap: The scp-style split behavior for multiple @ characters before the host/path colon is not defined.
contract_gaps.why_it_matters: An implementation could treat everything before the last @ as a login, reject it as an attempted password, or parse part of it as the host, with security and identity consequences.

contract_gaps.gap: The exact character set covered by “whitespace” and “trimming” is not stated.
contract_gaps.why_it_matters: ASCII-only trimming and language-native Unicode trimming can disagree on non-breaking spaces and other Unicode whitespace at security-sensitive prefixes.

contract_gaps.gap: Credential redaction specifies that the token must not appear, but does not define token boundaries or the rest of the error spelling.
contract_gaps.why_it_matters: Tests cannot honestly require a particular redaction placeholder or determine what substring must be hidden in more complex userinfo such as user:a:b@host.
